definition_zh: 冷酷无情的；麻木不仁的；起老茧的
definition_en: cruelly indifferent to the suffering of others; also (of skin) hardened and thickened
core_image: 一层厚茧盖住手掌，也盖住了心：摸到别人的疼痛却毫无感觉
scene: 老人摔倒在地，路人却面无表情地绕了过去，仿佛掌心结了茧，什么也感觉不到。The nurse was criticized for her callous attitude toward the patients.
sceneCN: 这里 callous 是「冷酷无情的」（第 2 个义项：对他人痛苦麻木不仁）；句意是这名护士因对病人态度冷漠而受到批评。

pos.zh: 冷酷无情的；麻木不仁的

derivatives.zh: 由形容词加副词后缀构成，义为「冷酷无情地」
由形容词加名词后缀构成，义为「冷酷无情；麻木不仁」
同源于拉丁词干 cal-（硬皮），义为「老茧；（植物）愈伤组织」
同源动词化用法，义为「使结茧；使变硬」

senses.title: Having hardened, thickened skin
senses.definition: covered with or transformed into hard, thick patches of skin, usually from repeated friction or work
senses.definitionCN: 皮肤因长期摩擦或劳作而长出又硬又厚的角质层
senses.example: Years of rowing left his palms callous and rough.
senses.exampleCN: 多年的划船让他的手掌长满老茧、粗糙不堪。
senses.why: The Latin root callos means hard skin, so the original sense is purely physical hardness on hands or feet.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词根 callos 本义是硬皮，所以最早的义项只是手或脚上物理性的硬化。

senses.title: Emotionally hardened and indifferent
senses.titleCN: 冷酷无情的；麻木不仁的
senses.definition: not feeling sympathy for others' suffering, as if the emotions themselves had grown a thick skin
senses.definitionCN: 对他人的痛苦没有同情心，仿佛情感本身也长出了一层厚茧
senses.example: It was callous of him to joke about the flood victims.
senses.exampleCN: 他拿洪灾受害者开玩笑，真是太冷酷了。
senses.why: The core image of a hard callus extends by metaphor from physical skin to emotional insensitivity.
senses.whyCN: 由「硬茧」的核心意象做隐喻延伸，从身体皮肤的硬化映射到情感的麻木。

senses.title: Made insensitive by repeated exposure
senses.titleCN: （因反复经历而）变得无动于衷的
senses.definition: having lost sensitivity to something because of overfamiliarity or repeated exposure
senses.definitionCN: 因为见得太多、经历太多次而对原本会触动人的事物失去敏感
senses.example: Constant bad news can leave people callous to tragedy.
senses.exampleCN: 源源不断的坏消息会让人对悲剧变得无动于衷。
senses.why: Just as friction thickens skin, repeated painful contact thickens feeling until nothing registers.
senses.whyCN: 就像摩擦让皮肤增厚一样，反复的痛苦接触让感受变钝，直到什么都激不起反应。

senses.title: Done without regard for others
senses.definition: showing cruel disregard for other people's welfare when acting or deciding
senses.definitionCN: 在做决定或行动时全然不顾他人的福祉与安危
senses.example: The company made a callous decision to cut safety funding.
senses.exampleCN: 公司做出了削减安全经费的冷酷决定。
senses.why: An indifferent feeling, once established, shows itself as actions that ignore others' welfare.
senses.whyCN: 麻木的心态一旦形成，就会外化为不顾他人福祉的行为。

senses.title: Unmoved by appeals to feeling
senses.titleCN: 不为所动的；铁石心肠的
senses.definition: remaining unaffected by pleading, pity, or emotional appeals
senses.definitionCN: 面对恳求、怜悯或情感诉求依然无动于衷
senses.example: She stayed callous even as the refugees told their stories.
senses.exampleCN: 即使难民们讲述自己的遭遇，她依然无动于衷。
senses.why: A hardened surface cannot be penetrated, so appeals of feeling simply fail to land.
senses.whyCN: 硬化的表面无法被穿透，因此情感诉求完全无法打动。

intro.en: Callous comes through Latin callosus from callum, hard skin; the jump from calloused hands to a calloused conscience took only a small metaphorical step.
intro.cn: callous 经由拉丁语 callosus 源自 callum（硬皮）；从「长茧的手」到「长茧的良心」，只走了小小的一步隐喻。

items.en: The reconstructed root *kal- / *klā- means hard or strong, giving a whole family of hardness words.
items.cn: 重构词根 *kal- / *klā- 意为「硬的、坚固的」，衍生出一整个「坚硬」词族。

items.en: Latin callum means hard skin or a callus, and the adjective callosus means thick-skinned or hard.
items.cn: 拉丁语 callum 指硬皮或老茧，形容词 callosus 意为皮厚的、坚硬的。

items.en: The word entered English in the sixteenth century as a medical term for hardened skin.
items.cn: 该词于十六世纪进入英语，最初是描述皮肤硬化的医学用语。

items.en: By the seventeenth century the metaphorical sense of emotional insensitivity was well established.
items.cn: 到十七世纪，「情感麻木」的比喻义已经完全确立。

items.en: Today the moral sense dominates usage, while the literal skin sense survives mainly in medical contexts; the noun callus remains the separate word for the hardened patch itself.
items.cn: 如今道德义占主导，字面的皮肤义主要留在医学语境；指硬皮本身的名词是另一个词 callus。

note.en: Callous is easy to confuse with its noun cousin callus and with similarly sounding words about hardness or coldness.
note.cn: callous 很容易和它的名词近亲 callus 以及一些发音或语义相近的词混淆。

entries.definition: The noun for a patch of hardened skin or healing bone tissue.
entries.definitionCN: 指硬皮斑块或骨痂的名词，与 callous 同根。

entries.definition: A genus of marsh plant, as in calla lily; only similar in sound.
entries.definitionCN: 马蹄莲属植物（如 calla lily 马蹄莲），只是发音相近，词源无关。

entries.definition: Inexperienced and immature; spelled and pronounced closely but from a different root.
entries.definitionCN: 稚嫩的、无经验的，拼写发音都很接近，但词源不同。

entries.definition: A formal noun for a callus, or for hardness of feeling.
entries.definitionCN: 正式用语，指老茧，也可指情感上的冷酷。

entries.definition: Showing no pity or compassion; unfeeling in a cruel way.
entries.definitionCN: 没有怜悯或同情心的，冷酷无情的。

entries.definition: Not showing or feeling sympathy or emotion.
entries.definitionCN: 不表露也感受不到同情或情感的。

entries.definition: Not aware of or considerate about others' feelings.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人的感受缺乏体察和顾忌的。

entries.definition: Showing no mercy or pity, often in punishment or judgment.
entries.definitionCN: 毫无怜悯、毫无慈悲的，常用于惩罚或评判场景。

entries.definition: Feeling and showing sympathy and concern for others.
entries.definitionCN: 对他人怀有并表现出同情与关怀的，是 callous 的反义对照。

normalIntro.en: Five memory hooks built on the cal- root of hardness and the shift from skin to soul.
normalIntro.cn: 五条围绕 cal-「坚硬」词根以及「从皮肤到心灵」引申路径的记忆钩子。

normal.en: Root cal- (Latin callum, hard skin) is the physical core: a callous hand is a hand with calluses.
normal.cn: 词根 cal-（拉丁语 callum，硬皮）是物理核心：callous 的手就是长满 callus（老茧）的手。

normal.en: Callous and callus differ by one letter: the adjective with -ous describes feelings, the plain noun names the patch of skin.
normal.cn: callous 与 callus 只差一个字母：带 -ous 的形容词形容心肠，光杆名词指那块硬皮。

normal.en: The same hardness family includes calliper- and caliber words of measure, all built on the idea of firmness.
normal.cn: 同一个「坚硬」家族还包括与测量相关的 caliber 等词，都建立在「坚实」的概念上。

normal.en: Collocate it with feelings: callous indifference and callous disregard are the standard exam pairings.
normal.cn: 搭配上记 feelings 方向：callous indifference 和 callous disregard 是考试高频组合。

normal.en: Medical texts keep the literal sense: a callous heel is a physical condition, not a moral judgment.
normal.cn: 医学文本保留字面义：callous heel 指脚跟皮肤硬化，不是道德评判。

abstract.en: Picture a heart wearing a thick leather glove: touches land on the glove, never on the heart.
abstract.cn: 想象一颗心戴着厚皮手套：所有触碰都落在手套上，永远到不了心。

abstract.en: Picture the road of hardship wearing grooves into a soul the way gravel wears calluses into feet.
abstract.cn: 想象苦难的路像碎石磨出脚茧那样，在灵魂上磨出一道道钝化的沟。

abstract.en: A callous person is a door with a padded frame: knocks of feeling make no sound inside.
abstract.cn: 冷酷的人像一扇装了软垫的门框：情感的敲门声传不进屋内。

examples.en: The landlord's callous refusal to fix the heating left tenants shivering all winter.
examples.cn: 房东冷酷地拒绝修理暖气，让租户整个冬天都在挨冻。

examples.en: Rowers and gymnasts often have callous palms from years of training.
examples.cn: 划船运动员和体操运动员因常年训练手掌上都有老茧。

examples.en: War reporters sometimes become callous simply to keep working.
examples.cn: 战地记者有时为了能继续工作而变得麻木。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「砍勒斯」——像被砍了一刀却毫无感觉的人，皮糙肉厚、麻木不仁；联想到手掌结了茧，被砍一下也只觉得勒斯（了事儿），便是冷酷无情。

root: 源自拉丁语 callum（硬皮、老茧），派生形容词 callosus（皮厚的、坚硬的），经十六世纪英语借入。词根 cal- 表示「硬」；本义指皮肤硬化，十七世纪起隐喻化为「情感上的麻木冷酷」。注意名词「老茧」英语用另一个词 callus。

sensesIntro.en: The senses run from literal hardened skin to metaphorical emotional hardness, then outward to insensitive acts and unresponsiveness.
sensesIntro.cn: 义项从字面的皮肤硬化出发，隐喻为情感上的硬化，再外化为无情的举动与不为所动的态度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a thick layer of hard skin that no touch can reach through.
core.cn: 核心意象：一层又厚又硬的皮，任何触碰都穿不透。

branches.en: THE BODY: calluses on hands and feet from work or friction.
branches.cn: 身体：劳作与摩擦在手脚上留下的老茧。

branches.en: THE SOUL: feeling itself thickens until suffering no longer registers.
branches.cn: 心灵：感受本身增厚变钝，痛苦再也激不起反应。

branches.en: CONDUCT: decisions and acts that ignore others' welfare.
branches.cn: 行为：不顾他人福祉的决定与举动。

branches.en: RESISTANCE: appeals and pleading that fail to move a hardened heart.
branches.cn: 抗拒：恳求与哀告打动不了铁石心肠。

branches.en: CONSEQUENCE: the social verdict on the person who does not feel.
branches.cn: 后果：社会对「感受不到他人痛苦之人」的谴责。

intro.en: Callous is built from the Latin root cal- (hard skin) plus the adjective suffix -ous, giving literally 'full of hardness'.
intro.cn: callous 由拉丁词根 cal-（硬皮）加形容词后缀 -ous 构成，字面意思是「充满坚硬之感的」。

latinIntro.en: The cal- root is small but productive, naming hardness on skin, in bone, and in measurement words.
latinIntro.cn: cal- 词根规模不大但很能产，涵盖皮肤、骨骼的硬化以及测量类词汇中的「坚实」概念。

items.example: Latin callum meant a patch of hard skin.
items.exampleCN: 拉丁语 callum 指一块硬皮。

items.meaning: full of, having the quality of
items.exampleCN: callosus 意为皮厚的、硬化的。

items.meaning: hardened skin patch; healing bone tissue
items.example: A callus formed on his fingers from guitar strings.
items.exampleCN: 吉他琴弦让他的手指上结了茧。

items.example: The essay attacked the callosity of official responses.
items.exampleCN: 文章抨击官方回应的冷酷。

items.meaning: to form or cause hardened skin
items.example: Manual labor callused his palms within months.
items.exampleCN: 几个月的体力活让他的手掌结了茧。

items.example: The memo callously blamed the victims.
items.exampleCN: 那份备忘录冷酷地把责任推给受害者。

items.meaning: the quality of being emotionally hardened
items.example: Her callousness shocked even her allies.
items.exampleCN: 她的冷漠连盟友都感到震惊。

items.example: 'Flea market' is a calque from French.
items.exampleCN: 「跳蚤市场」是源自法语的仿译词。

latinEntries.exampleCN: 农夫手上的老茧（拉丁语用例示意）
长满茧的手（拉丁语用例示意）
